Global summary

On 2026-07-07 the physical host running azlsapkaqdb06 (node 55f0378e-29d8-7595-d123-9f1dfa9a5046) developed a hardware fault (predicted memory failure — “1083 Samsung CB2 prediction”, crashes) and was marked Degraded → Unallocatable at 22:06. The Azure platform reacted by live-migrating the VM to a healthy node (4566616c-b55f-a597-da36-305020a925e9): placement at 22:17:21, an Infrastructure-initiated LiveMigration scheduled event (Freeze all) from 22:19:06 to 23:01:02. During the relocation the VM was restarted for ~1 minute (22:52:50→22:53:51) via a rebootful host-environment (node OS image) update, and the migration cutover froze the guest for ~2.581 s at 22:54; the migration Completed at 23:00:16 (root cause “UnallocatableNode / bad hardware health”). The faulty source node was subsequently Faulted (FaultCode 10038) and sent OutForRepair. This is a QA / non-production SAP database (application KAQ, SUSE SLES for SAP), but still SOX-regulated and Highly Restricted, so even a short pause plus a 1-minute restart is clearly noticed.

RCA candidate 1 — internal

Most likely explanation. The host node the VM was running on (55f0378e-29d8-7595-d123-9f1dfa9a5046) triggered a predicted memory hardware failure (Live Migration Events FailureReason “1083 Samsung CB2 prediction … RuleType: Failure Prediction”) and was declared NodeHealth Degraded → Unallocatable at 22:06 on 2026-07-07, later Faulted (FaultCode 10038) and OutForRepair. The platform reactively live-migrated the VM to healthy node 4566616c-b55f-a597-da36-305020a925e9 (container b03127fd-9c69-490e-bd49-b69f8fce73d2): placement 22:17:21, Infrastructure LiveMigration scheduled event 22:19:06–23:01:02 (Freeze all, estimated 5 min but actual ~42 min). The Scheduled Events & Reboots graph shows a reboot dot inside the scheduled-event bar: the VM was restarted 22:52:50→22:53:51 (~1 min), attributed by Reboot Detail to Planned.RootHEUpdate Rebootful.Out_of_band_HE_update_by_BatchingManager (a rebootful node-OS-image update, WAOS_WS19H ...20348.1075→...26102.1083) and by TM_RCA to Unplanned.ContainerFault.LiveMigration TriggerType,UnallocatableNode. The migration cutover then froze the guest for ~2.581 s at 22:54 and Completed at 23:00:16. IsCustomerInitiatedOperation=false, isGuestOsCrash=false — this was a platform-driven event, not a guest crash or a customer restart.

Customer context. azlsapkaqdb06 is a large-memory Standard_M128ds_v2 running SUSE SLES for SAP on Linux, tagged Azure SAP Non-prod / Stage=QA, application KAQ, Business_Criticality = 3 - less critical, but still SOX-regulated and Highly Restricted, administered by GTO SAP CTE DBA teams. Even though this is QA, a ~1-minute restart plus a ~2.6 s freeze is unambiguously visible; on clustered SAP DB workloads a live-migration blackout can also prompt a cluster manager (e.g. Pacemaker) to fence or fail over, which can surface as an additional unexpected stop.

Ruled-out factors. No regional outage overlapped the window. In-guest performance was not implicated: CPU mostly <5%, memory pressure stable at ~72–76%, RAM available stable, disk BW/IOPS in the low single digits. The only disk queue/latency spike (~145 / ~265 ms) occurred on 2026-07-09 ~06:00, well after the incident, and is not correlated.

Suggested further investigation. (1) Confirm the exact time the customer observed the restart and correlate against the 22:52:50–22:53:51 UTC reboot and the 22:54 cutover freeze. (2) Clarify with the Live Migration / Host-Environment teams whether the rebootful HE update was inherent to landing on the updated target host or a separately-scheduled concurrent update, since the 1-minute restart is the bulk of the customer-perceived impact. (3) Pull guest OS and SAP/cluster logs around 2026-07-07 22:50–23:01 UTC for fencing, failover or I/O-freeze messages. (4) Review why the migration ran ~42 min against a 5-min estimate (large 2 TB memory footprint).

RCA candidate 2 — customer-facing (draft)

Summary. On 7 July 2026, at approximately 22:52–22:53 UTC, your virtual machine was briefly restarted (about one minute) while the Azure platform relocated it to alternative, updated physical hardware as an automated protective maintenance action. Around the same window the virtual machine also experienced a very short pause of approximately two to three seconds during the relocation.

Root Cause. The physical host on which the virtual machine was running began to show early indicators of a hardware (memory) issue. To protect the workload, Azure automatically live-migrated the virtual machine to healthy hardware running an updated host platform. As part of moving to that updated hardware, the virtual machine underwent a brief restart, and the migration itself involved a short pause while memory and state were transferred. No platform outage was detected in the region during this period.

Resolution. The virtual machine was successfully relocated to healthy, updated hardware and the affected host was taken out of service for repair. No customer action is required, and the virtual machine has been operating normally since.

Customer Impact. A brief restart of approximately one minute, together with a short pause of a few seconds, around 22:52–22:54 UTC on 7 July 2026. For most workloads this is a brief, one-off interruption; however, sensitive clustered or high-availability database configurations may also react to such an event — for example by initiating a failover. We recommend reviewing application and cluster logs around this time to confirm whether any such failover was triggered.
